claims.claim: Kleander documents Kay's admitted 'telescoping' (iconoclasm moved centuries earlier; a 750-year Reconquista compressed to one lifetime) so that historical loss lands on the same set of characters and intensifies emotional response.
claims.source: Anya Kleander, 'Present Reality in Historical Fantasy' (Honours dissertation, University of Stirling, 2008)
claims.quote: intensify the emotional and intellectual response to what really happened

claims.claim: Kleander quotes Kay's stated method of a quiet, steady accumulation of detail and complexity that reaches readers subliminally and builds trust.
claims.source: Anya Kleander, 'Present Reality in Historical Fantasy' (Honours dissertation, University of Stirling, 2008)
claims.quote: quiet, steady accumulation of detail and complexity

claims.claim: Kleander observes that Kay plants hints to Valentin's identity as Rhun throughout Tigana which only make sense in retrospect.
claims.source: Anya Kleander, 'Present Reality in Historical Fantasy' (Honours dissertation, University of Stirling, 2008)
claims.quote: the hints only make sense in retrospect

claims.claim: Kleander notes that who survived the Ammar–Rodrigo duel is not revealed until halfway through the epilogue, by which point the outcome is 'strangely unimportant'.
claims.source: Anya Kleander, 'Present Reality in Historical Fantasy' (Honours dissertation, University of Stirling, 2008)
claims.quote: not until halfway through the epilogue that Kay reveals who survived

claims.claim: Kleander sets side by side two near-identical prayer paragraphs (Asharite and Jaddite) as the clearest example of Kay using structural repetition to show how alike the religions are.
claims.source: Anya Kleander, 'Present Reality in Historical Fantasy' (Honours dissertation, University of Stirling, 2008)
claims.quote: the clearest example of how alike the religions are

claims.claim: Kleander reads Pertennius (Procopius) as Kay's illustration that history is carved and chosen, with the narrator's opening line that writers of history seek the dramatic over the truth.
claims.source: Anya Kleander, 'Present Reality in Historical Fantasy' (Honours dissertation, University of Stirling, 2008)

claims.claim: Kleander (via Toolan) argues Kay's structure leaves the reader torn between different views rather than resolved.
claims.source: Anya Kleander, 'Present Reality in Historical Fantasy' (Honours dissertation, University of Stirling, 2008)

claims.claim: Rettino reads Tigana's first sentence ('In the autumn season of wine, word went forth...') as an entry in a chronicle lending historical flavour, then subverted when the reported death proves faked.
claims.source: Matthew Rettino, 'Fantasies of History: Guy Gavriel Kay's Synthesis of the Historical Fantasy Novel' (Honours thesis, McGill University, 2012)
claims.quote: reads like an entry in a chronicle

claims.claim: Rettino notes the narrator adopts a cautious, guessing persona ('perhaps because...') whose judgments the naive reader must nonetheless accept, the club-story authority of portal-quest fantasy.
claims.source: Matthew Rettino, 'Fantasies of History: Guy Gavriel Kay's Synthesis of the Historical Fantasy Novel' (Honours thesis, McGill University, 2012)
claims.quote: The narrator’s speculative persona supposedly only guesses

claims.claim: Rettino cites the Lions passage 'One hundred and thirty-nine citizens of Fezana... This was the way of it' as the omniscient historian's voice breaking the immersive character perspective.
claims.source: Matthew Rettino, 'Fantasies of History: Guy Gavriel Kay's Synthesis of the Historical Fantasy Novel' (Honours thesis, McGill University, 2012)

claims.claim: Rettino shows the narrator's voice and Jehane's thoughts intersecting so that distanced background exposition is disguised as the character's reflections.
claims.source: Matthew Rettino, 'Fantasies of History: Guy Gavriel Kay's Synthesis of the Historical Fantasy Novel' (Honours thesis, McGill University, 2012)

claims.claim: Rettino notes Jehane's noticing what is unusual, in free indirect discourse, dispenses world information without a guide figure.
claims.source: Matthew Rettino, 'Fantasies of History: Guy Gavriel Kay's Synthesis of the Historical Fantasy Novel' (Honours thesis, McGill University, 2012)
claims.quote: she notes, in free indirect discourse

claims.claim: Rettino argues that riselka prophecies foreshadow and expose the structural lines of Tigana, seams a mimetic novelist would hide.
claims.source: Matthew Rettino, 'Fantasies of History: Guy Gavriel Kay's Synthesis of the Historical Fantasy Novel' (Honours thesis, McGill University, 2012)
claims.quote: foreshadow and expose the structural lines in his novel

claims.claim: Rettino documents that Under Heaven's narrator speaks in several scenes in the voice of a later-dynasty historian, citing chroniclers' consensus and then departing from it with knowing irony.
claims.source: Matthew Rettino, 'Fantasies of History: Guy Gavriel Kay's Synthesis of the Historical Fantasy Novel' (Honours thesis, McGill University, 2012)
claims.quote: speaks in several scenes in the voice of a historian

claims.claim: Rettino points to the narrator's exclamation that Shen Tai 'hadn't even passed the examinations at that point!' as the moment author and historian-narrator blend.
claims.source: Matthew Rettino, 'Fantasies of History: Guy Gavriel Kay's Synthesis of the Historical Fantasy Novel' (Honours thesis, McGill University, 2012)
